findings.title: BuildIndex lost its exclusive lock; concurrent builds of the same key can race
findings.body: The change removes `b.cacheMu.Lock()` / `defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()` that previously wrapped the entire `BuildIndex` body and replaces it with only a tiny write-lock around `b.cache[key] = idx`. With the new code, two goroutines that both see a cache miss for the same `NamespacedResource` (e.g. concurrent `getOrCreateIndex` calls for the same key, which `search.go` already flags as a TODO) will both run `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for file-backed indexes at the same `filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", key.Resource, key.Group))`, both execute the builder, and race on the final cache write. The previous global lock was, perhaps inadvertently, also serializing same-key builds. The PR's stated goal is to allow different namespaces to build concurrently, but it should have used a per-key (or RWMutex-based) strategy instead of dropping the guard entirely; otherwise bleve may error out on the duplicate directory creation or two builds will silently overwrite each other in the cache.

findings.title: Init now starts the broadcaster after the search build, so events during build are dropped by both
findings.body: The order inside `s.once.Do` was changed from `initWatcher()` then `s.search.init(ctx)` to `s.search.init(ctx)` then `initWatcher()`. With the new ordering, any write that occurs while the search index is being built (which can take a long time) is no longer captured by the broadcaster — `initWatcher` hasn't started yet, and `searchSupport.init` only subscribes to `s.storage.WatchWriteEvents` after all builds complete. Before the change the broadcaster was already running and would buffer those events (also bumping `mostRecentRV`), so a Watch client connecting at startup would see them via `since`. After the change both the broadcaster and the search index miss events that happen during the build, and the broadcaster can lag behind the search index's own watch for the brief window between `WatchWriteEvents` being called in search.init and `initWatcher` actually running. The PR description does not mention this reordering; it should either be reverted or called out explicitly so reviewers can verify no caller relies on the broadcaster being live during the search build.

findings.title: Init failure is logged twice with the identical message
findings.body: `server.Init` already calls `s.log.Error("error initializing resource server", "error", s.initErr)` on failure, but `NewResourceServer` then logs the same error again with the identical message before returning: `s.log.Error("error initializing resource server", "error", err)`. The second log line is redundant and will produce duplicate `error initializing resource server` entries in the log for every init failure; one of the two should be removed.

findings.title: Integration test now skips postgres instead of being fixed
findings.body: The PR adds a `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` with a TODO to "fix this test for postgres". The test was presumably failing on Drone for postgres (which is a real CI environment), so the change converts a CI failure into silently-skipped coverage: no production combination is being exercised by this test for postgres any more. Either the test should be fixed for postgres or a tracking issue should be linked so the gap is not lost.
